about: The BCU1525's LiteDRAM core for 8 GB x8 UDIMMs without ECC (the opentpu card's, 2026-10-19: GOODRAM GR2400D464L17S/8G, DDR4-2400 CL17, one rank of eight 8 Gb x8 chips), one DDR4 channel per instance (otpu_ld4; the board top instantiates it once per DIMM channel C0..C3 when built with DIMM=udimm): USPDDRPHY (LiteDRAM's UltraScale+ PHY), 64 data bits, eight strobes (one per byte) and eight data masks (DM_n, on the RDIMM's upper-nibble strobe pins), at sys 150 MHz = DDR4-1200 (CL 9 from JEDEC's DDR4-2400R tAA 14.16 ns; the PHY's ISERDESE3s at 600 MHz: in component mode the -2 part's CLK takes 1.6 ns at least, and at DDR4-1600 their 800 MHz failed that pulse width check by 0.350 ns in every build; the 2026-10-26 card read no window on some lanes at 1600), two 512-bit native user ports (the even and the odd banks, straight through one register each way: ecc_ports.NativePortsPlain, with the ECC core's CSR names, enable 0), a BIST over 8 lanes, CSRs on an AXI-Lite slave in ctl_clk, and a VexRiscv (minimal) running LiteX's BIOS (lite console), which calibrates the channel at reset (mode registers, write leveling, read leveling; no RCD) and logs on serial_tx (115200 8N1); ready = cal_ready | the DFII's hardware control. Its clock input clk300 is the channel's 300 MHz clock on a global buffer. Generated by tools/litedram/gen_core_ddr4.py --dimm udimm (docs/bcu1525.md).

settings.toolchain: riscv64-elf-gcc 15.2.0 (Homebrew), run as riscv64-unknown-elf-* through a symlink shim (the Homebrew riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc's cc1 lacks libisl)
